findings: The diff is the plain union of the three source changes, and the author made no extra code edits. The parts are: the parallel combine/source for large perfect hash aggregates (E0003), the perfect hash join for RIGHT joins (E0004), partitioning count(DISTINCT) on the hash of the group keys (E0005), and the exact key-bitmap join filter with DELIM_GET pushdown (E0006). Every condition depends on general plan or data properties: estimated cardinality, key density, key type, memory limit, thread count, join type. None of them names a table, column or literal.

Checked whether the changes interfere with each other. The perfect hash join and the exact filter cannot both be active: CanUseBloomFilter (physical_hash_join.cpp:768) returns false when the hash table is perfect, so the bitmap is never built for a perfect join. The large perfect aggregate rejects DISTINCT aggregates (plan_aggregate.cpp), so it never overlaps with the distinct-HT partitioning. PropagateFoundMatches runs only when a perfect join executor exists and only for joins that propagate the build side.

Edge-case guards are in place. Exact mode: NULL keys are skipped on insert and follow filters_null_values on probe; an out-of-range key sets an overflow flag that lets everything pass; a mismatched key type lets everything pass; the bitmap is capped at 128 bits per key and 2^29 bits in total. Perfect join: NULL min/max is rejected and the duplicate check fixes the off-by-one. Large perfect aggregate: it is limited by density and by memory budget divided by threads.
